title: Stickball, Crescent Stars Park and the Negro league players
summary: Ball games on the greens and the old Crescent Stars Park, with pitcher Joe Perdo, Satchel Paige and Josh Gibson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. What kind of, uh, ball games did you play? They must have been not just baseball.

No, well, we had stick ball. You had stick ball. Stick ball. You hit, you hit your stick, your baseball bat might have been an old broom handle. Mm-hmm. Hit the ball, you run the first base, you had first, second and third base. Then sometimes as the, as the times went by, we would go out into the greens, which we used to call back of town. Back of town, back around St. Norton and Johnson, all those were big green lights. Mm-hmm. And a lot of the, a lot of the old baseball players, the Ray Bolton baseball players, before the Crescent Stalk Park was put up, they would play on the greens with the kids.
Mm-hmm. They, they got a kick out of them.

That's right. One of the real great pitches they had, it was a fella named Joe Pato. And, Pato, I think it's a P-E-R-D-O, I'm sure that's how you spell it. The old Thomas would remember that name. Mm-hmm. He, he would stop and, and play baseball with the kids, and with this old rag ball, and then leave them, go to Crescent Stalk Park, and pitch 18 innings against the great, great ball players. Mm-hmm. Buck Leonard, and, and, and, and, to name a few. Yeah. He'd be right in there, pitch 18 innings.
